8e509b1fb7.why: Old problems fixed. The doubling figure is gone; the card keeps only his ice-age cooling (CO2 cut to 0.62-0.55 cools 40-50 degrees latitude by 4-5 C, Le Moyne; AIP: halving cools Europe 4-5 C), told as his estimate ('enough, he thought'), so no forecast, warming amount or policy. The new lure 'Why some years are warmer than others' is live against the stem's 'warmer or colder' and wrong: the riddle of the ice ages set him to work (AIP, Grokipedia, his 1896 paper). 'Tedious calculations' is his own phrase. No tell, voice clean, no overlap.

bca954deb3.why: Old problem fixed: the key now claims only a rise from one year to the next, which two years of readings support (Scripps: the 1959 average had increased and 'increased still further in 1960'; AIP: by 1960 he reported a rising baseline). The key is no longer than the lures, and each lure is wrong (he found a clear seasonal cycle plus a rise). The card is the measured record only: 313 ppm first reading, every yearly average higher, about 430 ppm by early 2026. No forecast, no overlap.

f239f496c8.why: Old problem fixed: 'rocks such as limestone' now sets aside all rocks, so kerogen (about 15 million GtC) and the mantle (about 120 million GtC) are out, and the oceans (about 38,000 GtC, 'the largest active carbon reservoir') beat fossil fuels (5,000-10,000), soils plus plants plus permafrost (under about 4,700) and the air (about 900) (Grokipedia, Carbon cycle). Overlap: the stem only names the rock store as set aside; T3 why-earth-supports-life b25bf74134 still keys limestone, as the lead's ruling requires.

e706032189.why: The new question overstates the mechanism it applies. Dry desert air still holds all its carbon dioxide and some water vapour, and it still sends most of the ground's infrared back down. On a clear night the ground's net loss is 40-100 W/m2 (Grokipedia, Radiative cooling) against roughly 350-400 W/m2 emitted. A standard clear-sky (Brutsaert) estimate gives about 70 percent sent back in dry air, against about 85-90 percent in humid air. So the key's 'sends little of that heat back down' and the card's 'most of the ground's infrared escapes to space' are both false. PSU says only that dry air limits the amount of infrared the ground receives, and the unit's own first card has carbon dioxide sending heat back. Second problem: El Paso stands about 1,140 m up, so its air IS thinner than a lowland Southeast town's. The card's flat 'Dry air is not thinner than humid air' misleads for this town. The lure itself is still wrong, since rising warm air is not how the ground cools at night. Fix: key 'Its dry air sends less of that heat back down', and card 'more of the ground's infrared escapes to space'. Better also to drop 'thinner' from that lure, e.g. 'Its dry air lets warm air rise away faster'. Overlap cleared: T1 weather-and-climate-basics keys the word humidity (1e0d8ebf1a) and the sea breeze (f62f365e71), not night cooling. T3 heat-on-the-move keys radiation as a way heat travels, not back-radiation.
